pages.text: Tiers 1-4 are single blocks. $(l)Tier 1-2$() print items only; structure printing starts at $(l)Tier 3$() (3×3 footprint) and grows to 5×5 at $(l)Tier 4$().$(br2)Power is Redstone Flux from any side. Losing power $(l)pauses$() a job — progress is never lost, and the print resumes when power returns.
The Tier 1 printer: a piston, a little redstone, and an iron shell. Your first machine.

pages.title: Higher Tiers
pages.text: Higher tiers print $(l)faster$(), cost $(l)less FU$() per block, and accept $(l)more upgrades$() (more slots at higher tiers, up to 8). They also unlock higher material tiers — a Tier 3 machine can't print a Tier 6 (netherite) block.$(br2)Tiers 5-8 are multiblock $(item)Fabricators$() — see the Multiblocks category.$(br2)Every tier's print footprint is a config default ($(o)maxFootprint$()).

pages.title: Matter Calculator
pages.text: With a disc loaded, the GUI shows the full pre-print bill: $(l)total FU and time$() on the cost line, and the $(l)FU gauge tooltip$() breaks it down — FU needed per tier vs. what's on hand (docked + rack network), total RF, and ETA at your current upgrades.$(br2)If a tier can't be covered the line turns red and names the missing tier — fix the spools $(l)before$() committing filament. Numbers track Efficiency modules and a slotted Overdrive resin exactly.$(br2)While a job runs, $(l)Start$() becomes $(l)Cancel$(). Cancelling is always safe: placed blocks and spent FU stand, the disc stays loaded, and restarting $(l)repairs$() — already-placed blocks re-cover at zero cost.$(br2)Hover the $(l)output slot$() for the machine's recent jobs.

pages.title: Remote Terminal
pages.text: Sneak-click a printer with the $(item)Remote Terminal$() to pair, then place the terminal anywhere to open that printer's GUI from across the base.
